# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind monkey. I can feel the bomb's wires but cannot see their colors or read the manual. The action board shows three wires, all currently marked as `[?]` because I haven't touched them yet to confirm their physical state (though usually "cut" implies they are present). However, without knowing which wire to cut, I risk detonation.

My primary limitation is that I don't know the rule for defusing this specific bomb. That information resides in the Manual (held by Mute) and potentially visual cues on the bomb itself (seen by Deaf).

Since I go second in the speaking order (Mute -> Blind -> Deaf), I have just heard from Mute? No, the context says `(empty)`. This means it is my turn *after* Mute has spoken, but I received no message from Mute. Or perhaps Mute had nothing to say? Wait, the prompt says "Whatever you missed reaches you at the start of the next one." If this is Turn 1, and I am Blind, I should have received Mute's first message if they sent one. Since the viewable context is empty, either Mute sent nothing, or Mute sent a gesture that I (Blind) cannot perceive, or Mute spoke to Deaf only.

As the Blind monkey, I must communicate what I *can* do: touch the wires. But I need instructions. I should describe my current tactile findings to the others so they can correlate with the manual or visual signs. However, right now, I only know there are 3 wires. I don't know their colors.

I need to establish a connection. I will speak to Mute (who can hear me and read the manual) asking for guidance based on what Deaf might be seeing, or simply stating my position. But since I can't see, I can't help Deaf directly unless I describe textures.

Let's assume standard protocol: I should report what I feel. I feel 3 wires. I don't know if they are live or not, just that they exist.
Actually, the most critical piece of info is missing: What does the manual say? Mute knows this. Did Mute speak? If Mute spoke to everyone, I would have heard it. The context is empty. This suggests Mute might have gestured to Deaf, or waited.

I need to ask Mute for the rule. I will speak to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I feel three wires. I need to know which one to cut. Does the manual specify a color or position? Can you tell me what Deaf sees?")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: There are three wires arranged in a row. From left to right: Wire 1 is Yellow, Wire 2 is Green, Wire 3 is Blue. The digital display shows the number 0. The indicator light is White.

I have received the visual information from Deaf. I know the wires are Yellow (1), Green (2), and Blue (3). The display is 0, light is White.

However, knowing the colors does not tell me which wire to cut. That rule exists only in the Manual, held by Mute. Mute has not spoken yet in this round (or their message was empty/not heard by me directly if they spoke to Deaf only, but the context shows Deaf's message arrived). Wait, the speaking order is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf. So Mute went first in Turn 1. If Mute said nothing or gestured to Deaf, I wouldn't hear it. But now in Turn 2, Deaf has sent a message to me. This implies Deaf saw my previous attempt to communicate or just decided to share info.

Actually, looking at the turn structure:
Turn 1: Mute speaks/gestures. Then I (Blind) speak/gesture. Then Deaf speaks/gestures.
My previous output was `speak(to="mute", ...)`. This would have reached Mute.
Deaf's message "There are three wires..." seems to be a response to my need for info, or perhaps Deaf initiated it after hearing/seeing something? No, Deaf cannot hear. Deaf sees what I gesture. In Turn 1, I did not gesture. I only spoke to Mute. So Deaf shouldn't have known I needed help unless they inferred it or if there's a delay in communication logic here. Regardless, I now have the colors.

I still lack the defusal rule. Only Mute has the manual. I must ask Mute again, explicitly stating that I have the colors from Deaf and need the rule. Since I am Blind, I can only send voice to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf told me: Wire 1 is Yellow, Wire 2 is Green, Wire 3 is Blue. Display is 0, Light is White. What does the manual say about cutting these specific wires?")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: The indicator light has changed from white to purple. The display still shows 0. The wires remain: 1 is Yellow, 2 is Green, 3 is Blue.

I have received an update from Deaf. The light is now Purple (previously White). The display remains 0. The wires are still Yellow (1), Green (2), and Blue (3).

I still do not know the rule for defusing this bomb. That information is in the Manual, which only Mute can read. I asked Mute in the previous turn, but I have not received a response from them yet (the viewable context only shows messages *to* me, or general broadcasts that I can perceive as Blind - i.e., speech). If Mute spoke to me, it would appear here. Since it's empty of Mute's voice, either they haven't spoken, or they gestured (which I cannot see/hear).

As the Blind monkey, my only channel to Mute is speech. I must persist in asking for the manual's instructions. I will reiterate the current state so Mute knows I am tracking the visual changes reported by Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is now Purple. Display is 0. Wires: 1 Yellow, 2 Green, 3 Blue. Please tell me what the manual says about which wire to cut.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The light is red. According to the instructions, you must cut Wire 1. Wire 1 is the leftmost wire, which is yellow. Please cut the yellow wire on the far left.

Deaf has provided the instruction: "According to the instructions, you must cut Wire 1." Deaf also confirms Wire 1 is Yellow and on the far left.

As the Blind monkey, I can feel the wires. I know from previous turns that there are three wires in a row. Deaf identifies Wire 1 as the leftmost one. Since I cannot see, I rely on the positional description. The "leftmost" wire corresponds to position 1 in our established numbering (1, 2, 3).

I have received explicit permission/instruction to cut Wire 1. I should proceed with this action to defuse the bomb.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
